pois.intro: The Museum of Tomorrow is a science museum in the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It was designed by Spanish neofuturistic architect Santiago Calatrava, and built next to the waterfront at Pier Maua.

pois.name: Cristo Redentor
pois.intro: Christ the Redeemer is an Art Deco statue of Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, created by French-Polish sculptor Paul Landowski and built by Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa, in collaboration with French engineer Albert Caquot and Romanian sculptor Gheorghe Leonida who sculpted the face.

pois.name: Pão de Açúcar
pois.intro: Sugarloaf Mountain is a peak situated in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on a peninsula at the mouth of Guanabara Bay. Rising 396 m above the harbor, the peak is named for its resemblance to the traditional shape of concentrated refined sugarloaf.

pois.name: Corcovado
pois.intro: Corcovado is a mountain in central Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is a 710-metre granite peak located in the Tijuca Forest, a national park.

pois.name: Museu Nacional
pois.address: Quinta da Boa Vista, Rio de Janeiro, 20940-040
pois.intro: The National Museum of Brazil is the oldest scientific institution of Brazil. It is located in the city of Rio de Janeiro, where it is installed in the Paço de São Cristóvão, which is inside the Quinta da Boa Vista.

pois.name: Biblioteca Nacional
pois.address: 219 Avenida Rio Branco, Rio de Janeiro, 20040-008, BR
pois.intro: The National Library of Brazil is the depository of the bibliographic and documentary heritage of Brazil. It is located in Rio de Janeiro, the capital city of Brazil from 1763 to 1960, more specifically at Cinelândia square.

pois.name: Catedral de São Sebastião
pois.address: 245 Avenida República do Chile
pois.wikipedia: pt:Catedral de São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro
pois.intro: The Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Sebastian, better known as the Metropolitan Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro or as the Cathedral of St. Sebastian of Rio de Janeiro, is a cathedral of the Catholic Church and the seat of the Archdiocese of Rio de Janeiro.

pois.name: Sambódromo da Marquês de Sapucaí
pois.intro: The Sambadrome Marquês de Sapucaí is a purpose-built parade area built for the Rio Carnival in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The venue is also known as Passarela Professor Darcy Ribeiro or simply the Sambódromo in Portuguese or Sambadrome in English.

pois.name: Museu de Arte Contemporânea
pois.address: Mirante da Boa Viagem, Niterói, 24210-390
pois.wikipedia: pt:Museu de Arte Contemporânea de Niterói
pois.intro: The Niterói Contemporary Art Museum is situated in the city of Niterói, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and is one of the city’s main landmarks. It was completed in 1996.

pois.name: Marina da Glória
pois.intro: Marina da Glória is a marina located in the neighbourhood of Glória in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. This venue hosted the sailing events for the 2016 Summer Olympics within the Flamengo Park cluster, from 7 to 19 August 2016.

pois.name: Museu Nacional de Belas Artes
pois.address: 199 Avenida Rio Branco, Rio de Janeiro, 20040-008
pois.intro: The Museu Nacional de Belas Artes is a national art museum located in the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The museum, officially established in 1937 by the initiative of education minister Gustavo Capanema, was inaugurated in 1938 by President Getúlio Vargas.

pois.name: Jardim Botântico
pois.address: 1008 Rua Jardim Botânico, Rio de Janeiro, 22460-030
pois.wikipedia: pt:Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro
pois.intro: The Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden or Jardim Botânico is located at the Jardim Botânico district in the South Zone of Rio de Janeiro. The Botanical Garden shows the diversity of Brazilian and foreign flora.

pois.wikipedia: pt:Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Candelária
pois.intro: The Candelária Church is an important historical Roman Catholic church in the city of Rio de Janeiro, in southeastern Brazil. It was built and decorated during a long period, from 1775 to the late 19th century.

pois.name: Theatro Municipal

pois.wikipedia: pt:Teatro Municipal do Rio de Janeiro
pois.intro: The Theatro Municipal is an opera house in the Centro district of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Built in the early twentieth century, it is considered to be one of the most beautiful and important theaters in the country.

pois.address: Praça Marechal Âncora, Rio de Janeiro

pois.name: Arcos da Lapa
pois.intro: The Carioca Aqueduct, also known as Arcos da Lapa, is an aqueduct in the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The aqueduct was built in the middle of the 18th century to bring fresh water from the Carioca River to the population of the city.

pois.name: Paço Imperial
pois.address: 48 Praça Quinze de Novembro, Rio de Janeiro, 20010-010
pois.intro: The Paço Imperial, or Imperial Palace, previously known as the Royal Palace of Rio de Janeiro and Palace of the Viceroys, is a historic building in the center of the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The Paço Imperial was built in the 18th century to serve as a residence for the governors of colonial Brazil.

pois.name: Museu de Arte Moderna (MAM)
pois.address: 85 Avenida Infante Dom Henrique, Rio de Janeiro, 20021-140
pois.wikipedia: pt:Museu de Arte Moderna do Rio de Janeiro
pois.intro: The Museum of Modern Art of Rio de Janeiro is a museum located in northeastern Flamengo Park, in the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is in the Centro district, west of Santos Dumont Airport, on Guanabara Bay.

pois.name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Monte do Carmo
pois.address: Rua Primeiro de Março, Rio de Janeiro, 20010-000
pois.wikipedia: pt:Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Monte do Carmo
pois.intro: The Old Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro dedicated to Our Lady of Mount Carmel is an old Carmelite church which served as cathedral of Rio de Janeiro from around 1808 until 1976. During the 19th century, it was also used successively as Royal and Imperial Chapel by the Portuguese Royal Family and the Brazilian Imperial Family, respectively.

pois.name: Monumento Nacional aos Mortos da Segunda Guerra Mundial
pois.address: 75 Avenida Infante Dom Henrique, 20021-140
pois.wikipedia: pt:Monumento aos Mortos da Segunda Guerra Mundial
pois.intro: The Monument to the Dead of World War II, also the Monument to the Brazilian Soldiers of World War II, popularly known as Monumento aos Pracinhas commemorates Brazil's participation and losses in the Second World War. It is located in Flamengo Park on Guanabara Bay, in the Flamengo neighborhood of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

pois.name: Museu da República
pois.address: 153 Rua do Catete, Rio de Janeiro, 22220-000
pois.intro: The Catete Palace is an urban mansion in the Flamengo neighborhood of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The property stretches from Rua do Catete to Praia do Flamengo.

pois.name: Museu Carmem Miranda
pois.address: Avenida Rui Barbosa, 22250-020
pois.intro: The Carmen Miranda Museum, located in Brigadeiro Eduardo Gomes Park, is dedicated to honoring the life and career of singer and actress Carmen Miranda. Open to the public since 1976, the museum was officially inaugurated on the 21st anniversary of her death.

pois.name: AquaRio
pois.address: Praça Muhammad Ali, Rio de Janeiro, 20220-360
pois.intro: The Marine Aquarium of Rio de Janeiro, or AquaRio, is a public aquarium located in the Gamboa neighborhood, in the port zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. With a constructed area of about 26,000 square metres, it is located to the west of Muhammad Ali Square.

pois.name: Praça Quinze de Novembro
pois.wikipedia: pt:Praça Quinze de Novembro (Rio de Janeiro)
pois.intro: The Praça XV de Novembro, is a public square in the Centro section of the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. In addition to being located on Rua Primeiro de Março, the square is part of Orla Conde, a public promenade that runs along Guanabara Bay.

pois.name: Aterro do Flamengo
pois.intro: Flamengo Park, also known as Aterro do Flamengo, Eduardo Gomes Park, and Aterro do Brigadeiro Eduardo Gomes, is the largest public park and recreation area within the city of Rio de Janeiro, in eastern Brazil, and the largest urban seaside park in the world. [1] The park is located along Guanabara Bay, in the Flamengo neighborhood of the city, between Downtown Rio and Copacabana.

pois.name: Campo de Santana
pois.wikipedia: pt:Campo de Santana (Parque do Rio de Janeiro)
pois.intro: The Campo de Santana is a park located in the Praça da República in downtown Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The name of the plaza refers to the fact that it is located near the site where Brazil was declared a republic in 1889.

pois.name: Praça Mauá
pois.intro: Praça Mauá is a square situated in the Centro neighborhood of the Zona Central of Rio de Janeiro. With an area of 25,000 m2, it is part of the Orla Conde, a public sidewalk that runs alongside Guanabara Bay.

pois.name: Quinta da Boa Vista
pois.intro: The Quinta da Boa Vista is a public park of great historical importance located in the São Cristóvão neighbourhood, in the North zone of the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

pois.name: Morro da Conceição
pois.intro: El Morro da Conceição es un accidente geográfico de la ciudad de Río de Janeiro, Brasil.

pois.name: Morro de Santo Antônio
pois.intro: El Morro de Santo Antônio es un accidente geográfico ubicado en la ciudad de Río de Janeiro, Brasil. Se encuentra adyacente al Largo da Carioca.

pois.name: Ilha Fiscal
pois.intro: Ilha Fiscal, or Fiscal Island, is an island in Guanabara Bay, bordering the historic city center of Rio de Janeiro, in southeastern Brazil. Originally named by Europeans as Rat Island, its current name comes from the fact that the customs department has been stationed there before Guarda Fiscal, serving the port of the then-capital of the Empire during the nineteenth century.

pois.name: Bio Parque do Rio
pois.address: Parque Quinta da Boa Vista, Rio de Janeiro
pois.intro: The Rio de Janeiro Zoological Garden is a zoo located in the district of São Cristóvão, in the municipality of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The institution has among its main objectives the development of environmental and educational activities, based on the animals of its collection—which consists mainly of fish, reptiles, birds, and mammals.

pois.name: Palácio Tiradentes
pois.address: Rua Primeiro de Março, Rio de Janeiro, 20010-090
pois.intro: The Tiradentes Palace is an eclectic government building located in the Centro neighborhood, next to the Paço Imperial in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It was inaugurated on 6 May 1926 and was the former seat of the Chamber of Deputies of Brazil, between 1926 and 1960, and is the current seat of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Rio de Janeiro.

pois.name: Edifício A Noite
pois.address: Praça Mauá, Rio de Janeiro, 20090-00
pois.intro: The Joseph Gire Building, better known as the A Noite Building or Edificio o Jornal A Noite, is an office building located in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil that served as the headquarters of the Rio-based newspaper A Noite. At a height of 102 meters, it was the tallest building in Brazil for two years between 1927 and 1929 before it was surpassed by the Martinelli Building in São Paulo.

pois.name: Morro da Saúde
pois.intro: El Morro da Saúde es un accidente geográfico de la ciudad de Río de Janeiro, Brasil.

pois.name: Passeio Público
pois.intro: The Passeio Público is a public park in the historic centre of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Built after 1779, it is the oldest public park of Brazil and one of the oldest in the Americas.

pois.name: Memorial dos Pretos Novos
pois.intro: Der Cemitério dos Pretos Novos, deutsch Friedhof der neuen Schwarzen, auch Memorial dos Pretos Novos genannt, ist ein Begräbnisplatz in Rio de Janeiro mit Massengräbern für umgekommene Sklaven.

pois.name: Morro da Babilônia
pois.intro: The Morro da Babilônia is a hill in the Leme neighbourhood of Rio de Janeiro, separating Copacabana beach from Botafogo. It is home to a favela known by the same name, as well as the favela Chapéu Mangueira.

pois.name: Escadaria Selarón
pois.address: Rua Manoel Carneiro
pois.intro: Escadaria Selarón, locally known as the 'Lapa Steps' for being situated at the "Lapa" neighborhood, is a set of world-famous steps in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. They are the work of Chilean-born artist Jorge Selarón who claimed it as "my tribute to the Brazilian people".
